;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Operation Barkhane]]
***Ten [[Malian soldier]]s are killed during an [[ambush]] in [[Nara, Mali|Nara]], [[Koulikoro Region|Koulikoro]], [[Mali]]. The attackers placed mines, which caused explosions after the army's vehicle passed, and then opened fire against the soldiers. [https://www.koaci.com/article/2020/09/04/mali/politique/mali-10-soldats-dont-un-sous-lieutenant-tues-dans-une-embuscade-pres-de-nara_144672.html (Koaci)]
***Two [[French Army|French]] soldiers are killed when their [[Armoured fighting vehicle|armoured vehicle]] hits an [[Improvised explosive device|IED]] in [[Kidal Region]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200905-two-french-soldiers-killed-in-mali (France 24)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Clashes between armed civilians and [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] militants leaves 14 civilians and 16 militants dead in [[Galmudug]], central [[Somalia]]. They began when the [[Islamist]] militants demanded villagers surrender their weapons and [[livestock]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/09/dozens-dead-central-somalia-villagers-battle-al-shabab-200905135828647.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Pacific typhoon season]]
**Typhoon Haishen approaches [[Japan]], threatening the coasts of [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]] and the island of [[Kyushu]]. Chief Cabinet Secretary [[Yoshihide Suga]] says the [[government of Japan|government]] is setting up a crisis response team and urges people to take precautions. Officials compare the typhoon to [[Typhoon Vera]], which in 1959 killed more than 5,000 people. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/japan-bracing-dangerously-powerful-typhoon-72813325 (ABC News)]
**The ''[[Rodong Sinmun]]'' reports that the [[North Korean government]] has "punished" local officials for failing to evacuate residents amid the [[landfall]] of [[Typhoon Maysak (2020)|Typhoon Maysak]], resulting in a "serious incident" involving numerous casualties. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2020/09/22c798e1a21f-n-korea-punishes-officials-after-typhoon-casualties.html (Kyodo News)]
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**The [[El Dorado Fire]] grows to {{convert|800|acres|ha}}, prompting emergency evacuations in [[Oak Glen, San Bernardino County, California|Oak Glen]], [[Mountain Home Village, California|Mountain Home Village]], [[Yucaipa, California|Yucaipa]], and [[Forest Falls, California|Forest Falls]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/california-wildfire-oak-glen-evacuated (Fox News)] [https://www.desertsun.com/story/news/2020/09/05/oak-glen-residents-ordered-evacuate-400-acre-wildfire-burns-rapid-rate/5729799002/ (''The Desert-Sun'')]
**The [[Pacific Gas and Electric Company]] warns customers that power could be shut off in some areas of [[California]] due to extreme weather and high winds. [https://www.mercurynews.com/2020/09/05/pge-warns-of-possible-power-shutoff-next-week-due-to-extreme-weather-high-wind/ (''The Mercury News'')]
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**Two more people in [[Louisiana]] die from [[Hurricane Laura]], bringing the statewide death toll to 25. A 52-year old man in [[Grant Parish, Louisiana|Grant Parish]] died from heat-related illness while removing storm debris, and a 25-year old man in [[Natchitoches Parish, Louisiana|Natchitoches Parish]] died from electrocution. [https://time.com/5886488/hurricane-laura-death-toll-louisiana/?ocid=uxbndlbing (''Time'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
*****More than 20 students at [[New York University]] are suspended for violating their COVID-19 policies. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/more-20-nyu-students-suspended-breaking-coronavirus-rules-school-says-n1239443 (NBC News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts]]
*****[[Northeastern University]] dismisses 11 students for violating COVID-19 guidelines. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/northeastern-dismisses-11-students-for-violating-covid-19-policies/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hawaii]]
****[[Hawaii County, Hawaii|Hawaii County]] closes their beaches and shoreline parks through September 19 in an effort to stop the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.staradvertiser.com/2020/09/05/hawaii-news/hawaii-county-to-close-beaches-parks-through-sept-19/ (''The Honolulu Star-Advertiser'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi]]
*****[[Delhi]] records 2,973 cases, the city's highest since June 26. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/covid-19-delhi-records-highest-spike-in-cases-in-71-days-death-count-4538/articleshow/77952921.cms (''The Times of India'')]
****India surpasses four million cases after reporting 86,432 new infections in the past 24 hours. The [[Ministry of Health and Family Welfare|health ministry]] also reports 1,089 deaths for a total of 69,561. [https://apnews.com/f6ffdffc37e3322eb7f3ea87cd0f130d (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Education in Iran|Schools]], including [[Hawza|Islamic seminaries]], reopen to some 15 million students after a seven-month closure. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6911720/iran-schools-reopen-despite-virus-concerns/?cs=14264 (AAP via ''The Canberra Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****510 cases in South Korea are linked to anti-[[Government of South Korea|government]] protests. [https://edition.cnn.com/world/live-news/coronavirus-pandemic-09-05-20-intl/h_3bc2d2ebfff9be2306d13b44c5657789 (CNN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[South Africa]] is expected to begin a trial of the NVX-CoV2373, a [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] candidate produced by [[Novavax]]. Around 2,904 volunteers are expected to be selected, who are aged from 18 to 64 years. [https://www.myjoyonline.com/news/health/south-africa-begins-trial-of-second-covid-19-vaccine/ (MyJoyOnline)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
***[[Portugal]] reports 486 cases, their biggest increase since their [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] was lifted in May. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-portugal-idUSKBN25W0RY (Reuters)]
*[[Climate movement]]
**[[Environmental activist]]s of the [[Extinction Rebellion]] movement in England gather around several printing presses used by the [[Rupert Murdoch]]-owned publishing company [[News Corp (2013–present)|News Corp]] in the towns of [[Broxbourne]], [[Hertfordshire]], and [[Knowsley, Merseyside]], criticising the [[Media coverage of global warming|coverage of global warming]] by News Corp-owned [[List of newspapers in the United Kingdom|newspapers]]. At least 34 protesters are arrested, while the protests lead to delays in the dissemination of the newspapers. [https://www.dw.com/en/extinction-rebellion-blockades-murdoch-owned-plants/a-54824580 (DW)] [https://www.smh.com.au/environment/climate-change/rupert-mudoch-s-british-newspapers-delayed-as-extinction-rebellion-protesters-stop-the-presses-20200905-p55sqr.html (Reuters via ''The Sydney Morning Herald'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***Twenty unmasked protesters are arrested during anti-lockdown protests at the [[Shrine of Remembrance]] in [[Melbourne]]. [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/multiple-arrests-as-hundreds-of-people-protest-victoria-s-coronavirus-lockdown (SBS)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
***[[Israelis]] protest against [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] for his response to the outbreak as cases increase in the country, as well as calling for his [[resignation]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/israelis-protest-pm-coronavirus-infections-spike-72840220 (ABC News)] 
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**Opposition activist [[Olga Kovalkova]] flees to [[Poland]] after her release from prison. Kovalkova reported that authorities warned her of further arrests if she did not leave the country. Kovalkova had been sentenced to 10 days in prison on August 25. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-belarus-election-poland-kovalkova/belarusian-opposition-activist-kovalkova-leaves-country-after-arrest-idUSKBN25W0OU?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Killing of Daniel Prude]]
**The fourth night of protests in [[Rochester, New York]], over the death of Daniel Prude, becomes the largest so far, and again it ends with pepper balls, tear gas, and fireworks. [[Rochester Police Department]] arrests nine people, including two on felony charges. Three officers are also treated at the hospital for injuries. A [[U-Haul]] truck [[Arson|is set on fire]] in a parking lot before firefighters arrive to put it out.  [https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/news/2020/09/05/daniel-prude-rochester-ny-black-lives-matter-protests-justice-police/5732337002/ (''The Democrat & Chronicle'')]

;Sports
*[[2020 Kentucky Derby]]
**The 146th [[Kentucky Derby]] is held after being delayed for four months due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In an upset, racehorse [[Authentic (racehorse)|Authentic]] wins the Derby over the favored [[Tiz the Law]], precluding the latter's chances of winning this year's [[Triple Crown of Thoroughbred Racing (United States)|Triple Crown]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/09/05/kentucky-derby/?outputType=amp (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.wlky.com/article/there-will-be-no-triple-crown-winner-in-2020/33933347 (WLKY-TV)]
